newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks end down, focus on suspensions.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks end down, focus on suspensions.

text.p: Jakarta stocks ended down on Friday due to worries over the rupiah and likelihood of poor first half earnings, but the focus was on the bourse's suspension of two stocks for sharp fluctuations, brokers said.
The Jakarta composite index ended 1.99 points, or 0.28 percent, lower at 710.06 points. Decliners led advancers by 70 to 42 with 73 issues unchanged.
Total turn-over was estimated at 495 billion rupiah.
"Sentiment was weak due to worries over the rupiah and poor earnings... The market focus was on the exchange's decision to suspend two small stocks," one broker said.

The rupiah, which has been volatile after plunging to a record low against the dollar on Monday, was likely to weaken in the short-term despite the country's strong economic fundamentals, economists said.
Spot rupiah, however, was relatively stable in late trading. It was quoted at 2,608/14 at 0940 GMT compared with an opening of 2,601/09.
Brokers said the market focus was on plastics manufacturer Langgeng Makmur and Bank Papan following the exchange's decison to suspend the two small stocks.
Bank Papan was suspended after a sharp rise, while Langgeng was suspended due to a sharp drop, an exchange official said.
Bank Papan was up 375 rupiah at 2,000 rupiah in thin trading, with only 179,500 shares traded before it was suspended at around 0730 GMT, an exchange official said.
Langgeng Makmur fell 275 rupiah to 975 rupiah, with some 4.9 million shares traded, before it was suspended at around 0850 GMT, shortly before the close of trading, the official said.
"This time the suspension was due to sudden sharp drop. Last Tuesday, Langgeng was temporarily suspended due to a sudden sharp rise," the official said.
Brokers praised the exchange's move, but said authorities should get tougher and investigate details such as finding out who was behind the sharp rise and their motives so as to prevent recurrences.
Pharmaceutical stocks Darya Varia, Kalbe Farma and Tempo Scan were among the losers due to weak sentiment on the sector.
Sentiment on the sector was negative after Kalbe's announcement of only a slight increase in its first half net profit and expected poor earnings from Darya, brokers said.
Newly-listed Lippo Cikarang was the most active, with some 25 million shares traded.
Lippo Cikarang rose 25 rupiah to 1,150 rupiah.
